title: Cheat meals reality check
summary: NH distinguishes planned refeeds (aimed at performance) from cheat meals (aimed at feeling better) and argues cheat meals signal an overly strict, emotionally abusive relationship with diet. Binges are mostly stored as fat, stress digestion and create psychological dependence; he instead eats foods he enjoys every day from a large repertoire of home-cooked whole foods.

claims.claim: Refeeds are planned with one goal, fueling performance; cheat meals are designed to make you feel better and make dieting easier, which is the problem.
Cheat meals are a staple of bro culture in France and are resurging in the US through 10k-calorie and junk food challenges.
A typical cheat meal is very high in calories with distorted macros: lots of carbs and fat, less protein than you think, few micronutrients, lots of sodium and trans fats.
If your diet is so strict you need a weekly junk binge to stay sane, rethink the diet; it's like an abusive relationship with your food.
The body can't use a huge one-day surplus to build muscle; what it can't use for muscle is stored as fat, and a previously depleted body may waste even more of it.
A weekly binge after restriction does refill glycogen, but rich food once a week also stresses the stomach and skin.
Cheat meals create psychological dependence and make you hate your diet while waiting for the one day you eat what you like; eat things you like every day instead.
Tasty food doesn't automatically have bad macros; many home-made whole foods are delicious and sustainable, though highly palatable foods tend to be higher in fat and calories.
NH never does cheat days: every day is a cheat day because he only eats food he enjoys, avoids processed food and distorted macro ratios, and is very happy with his diet.
Through years of experimenting he has so many food options that for any nutrient he can think of 10 dishes to make himself.
A sustainable diet requires doing your own grocery shopping and cooking; meal-prepping dry chicken and rice then bingeing on Sunday is a weak-minded approach.
Diet must be something you can repeat for the rest of your life; anything you dislike won't be consistent for years.
